target_customer: African SMEs and startups, mainly in Nigeria and Kenya, with finance teams managing spending, payroll and payments
problem: African businesses lack integrated tools for corporate cards, expense approval, payroll and multi-currency payments, so spending is hard to control and track.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription plus payments and card revenue, with banking provided by licensed partner banks
product_category: Spend management and corporate cards for African businesses

founders.name: Achille Arouko
previous_startups: Described as a three-time founder in fintech and AI; names not given
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; TechCrunch reports he conceived the idea at Paystack after seeing how BILL Spend and Expense handled company cards.

founders.name: Samy Chiba
education: Two MSc degrees in Business Administration
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; joined at the pivot to B2B per a search summary.

competitors.name: Allawee
competitors.what: Financial control platform for African businesses

competitors.name: Brass
competitors.what: B2B neobank in Nigeria; per TechCabal in 2023 it did not issue business cards or offer robust expense management

technical_complexity.rationale: Card issuing, payments and payroll across currencies rely on partner banks and integrations; hard parts are compliance and reconciliation rather than novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Finance workflows and bank partnerships create some lock-in, but features are replicable and rivals like Allawee, Duplo and Flex Finance target the same buyers.

incumbents: Global platforms such as Ramp and Brex
takeover_risk_then.outcome: Local banks and fintechs competed for SME finance; one rival, Brass, announced it would stop operating independently in 2026 per a sponsored partner post. No acquisition of Bujeti found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch coverage says the founder saw the pain at Paystack and that nearly 1,000 businesses onboarded within eight weeks of the 2023 raise, indicating demand; no independent market sizing was gathered.

identity.voice_and_tone: Professional finance voice, now with an AI layer called BRAIN

brand_strength.rationale: Regular African tech press coverage (TechCabal, Techpoint) of the company, but no source on the brand itself or community; the name appears to echo budget but that is unconfirmed.

pivots.from: Personal finance app for the African diaspora to automate remittances
pivots.to: B2B expense management for African businesses
pivots.why: Not stated in the source; YC page says the company pivoted to B2B

outcome_analysis: Bujeti began as a diaspora personal finance app and pivoted to B2B spend management in 2022, then joined YC in Winter 2023. It raised a $2M seed led by Y Combinator in December 2023, onboarded about 1,000 businesses within eight weeks and later reported 5,000 finance professionals across Nigeria and Kenya. A founder with Paystack experience and a pivot into a clearer need explain the traction, while no later round has been found.
notes: Seed confirmed by TechCrunch and Techpoint. CB Insights and Caplight list 2.5M total over 3 rounds, unreconciled. Founding year conflicts (2021 per YC and CB Insights, 2022 elsewhere). Competitor list limited to rivals named in a March 2023 TechCabal piece; Duplo, Flex Finance and Boya appear in undated reports and are not listed. Founder education for Achille not found.
